theorem: Klein Quartic Substrate Closure Theorem.  At the W(3,3) saturation point q = 3, the Klein quartic X(7) is the unique genus-q Hurwitz-extremal Riemann surface.  Its five classical invariants are all substrate primitives: Weierstrass points = f, bitangents = n_even (spine staircase), sextactic points = 2^q * Phi_6, Hurwitz orbits = mu * T_6 = Csaszar flag count, and |Aut| = f * Phi_6 = Hurwitz bound 84(q-1).  The sum of the four non-automorphism invariants is 24 + 28 + 56 + 84 = 192, which EQUALS the tomotope flag count (24 + 84 + 84) and the Weyl group order |W(D_4)| (24-cell symmetry).  Three independent pictures -- classical algebraic geometry of the Klein quartic, discrete oscillator-flag census of the tomotope, and the Weyl group of the 24-cell -- all evaluate to 192 in substrate form.
